hindi: अब इसलिए हम शरीर सम्बन्धी दूतादिविज्ञानीय यानी दूत आदि के ज्ञान का व्याख्यान करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the Dūtādivijñānīya (knowledge of the messenger and the rest), belonging to the body (śārīra).
notes: The title can be read 'what is to be known about the messenger and so on'. 'śārīram' is read as an attribute of the subject-matter (the section on the body, Śārīrasthāna); the noun it agrees with is not stated and none is supplied. The unit is a single printed line.

hindi: रिष्ट यानी मृत्यु के निकट होने का लक्षण, जो रोगी पर आश्रित है, बताया जा चुका है।
english: Riṣṭa (a sign of approaching death), which rests on the patient, has been indicated.
notes: riṣṭa = sign of impending death (standard). 'āturāśrayam' is read as one bahuvrīhi qualifying riṣṭam (patient-based); alternatively 'āturāśrayam' (the patient's support) could be a separate noun; the first reading is the more natural. 'nirdiṣṭam' is a past participle with no auxiliary (none supplied beyond English 'has been'). The token 'riṣṭamāturāśrayaṃ' is a single printed word without a space (split read from sense).

notes: GROUPING: one long sentence; the subject 'dūtaḥ' comes near the end (dūto vaidyam upasarpan aśubhaḥ). The giant compound 'tṛṇa...sneha-bhājana-dharaḥ' is printed as one word ending in -dharaḥ (bearer, holder) and is rendered as a list in the printed order; the body parts inside it (head, nose, ..., lower leg) sit oddly with 'bearer', and 'spṛk' (possibly 'touching') suggests the original may have listed things touched, but this is not certain and no verb is supplied. The printed 'loṣṭupāṃgāra' is read as loṣṭa + aṅgāra (charcoal), which does not match the print letter for letter (the letters 'u' and 'pā' are dropped; loṣṭa + pāṃsu 'dust' + aṅgāra is another possible guess), and 'mārjanośastra' as mārjana + ūṣa (saline soil) + śastra; both are conjectural. 'pala' is flesh (pala can also be a measure); 'kapāla' skull or potsherd. 'pādābhyāṃ bhuvaṃ muñcan' is rendered literally, its sense is unclear. 'vyādhino' is a doubtful form (vyādhin nominative would be vyādhī); read as 'diseased'. 'neko' (before jīrṇa) has a visarga-o for which the compound gives no reason; 'aneka' is rendered 'of many kinds'. 'varṇottama' read as 'higher in varṇa than the patient'. jaṅghā = lower leg per glossary.

english: Likewise, at midday, at both twilights, at midnight (on a conjectural reading), on the fourth, sixth and ninth lunar days, on parva days, on seeing an eclipse (uparāga) of a graha or portents (utpāta), and under the nakṣatras Bharaṇī, Kṛttikā, Ārdrā, Āśleṣā, Maghā, Mūla and the Pūrvā ones, (one) is inauspicious; and he who approaches the physician when he is asleep, naked, lying on the ground, anointed with oil, with loosened hair, facing south, agitated, cutting, breaking, inclined to fire-rites and rites for the ancestors, thinking and speaking what is inauspicious; or he who, having made an añjali toward the southern direction, stands on one foot, unevenly; and when the messenger is telling the abode of the patient, if the physician notices an inauspicious sense-object or imagines one, he should not follow him.

'yasmin ... dūte kathayati' is read as a locative absolute. vyādhitāśraya may be the patient's dwelling or the part of the body that is diseased. 'ārdrārātri' (wet night?) is read as ardha-rātri (midnight), conjecturally, since the nakṣatra Ārdrā is named separately in the next token; 'madhyānho' is a letter inversion for madhyāhna. english: Birds with male names, on the left, are auspicious; śivā (probably the she-jackal), śyāmā, piṅgalā, kokilā (cuckoo), an unclear word (ralā), the musk shrew (chuchundarī), the sow, the house lizard and single-hoofed animals, having female names, are auspicious on the right; the peacock, bear, śrīkaṇṭha and dog, thus, not; the elephant, the goat and payas (milk or water) also; but at entering they are reversed. And everywhere, on a conjectural reading, the going of a dog and a jackal from the right to the left is undesired; the reverse for beasts and birds.

lines_deva: शशसर्पाजाऽविगोधराजाहकमूकराणां तु कीर्तनमिष्टं न दर्शनं विरुतं चविपरीतंमृक्षवानरयोः

words.gloss: of chameleon (saraṭa; probable), fowl, cat, owls

hindi: सरट यानी सम्भवतः गिरगिट या बगीचे की छिपकली, मुर्गे, बिल्ली और उल्लुओं का तो सब कुछ ही अनिष्ट है।
english: But everything of the saraṭa (probably the chameleon or garden lizard), fowl, cat and owls is undesired.
notes: 'sarvam' presumably covers sight, mention and cry from the preceding units; this is not stated and is not added. saraṭa = chameleon or garden lizard (probable); kukkuṭa = fowl (glossary); viḍāla = cat; ulūka = owl. The printed 'viḍāḻa' has ḷ for l (print habit, normalised).

words.gloss: in nodules (granthi), tumours (arbuda) and so on
in gulma (abdominal lump), udara (abdominal disease; probable) and so on
in diarrhoea (atisāra), raktapitta (a bleeding disorder) and so on
in urinary stone (aśmarī), udāvarta (upward-turning of wind) and so on

hindi: इसी प्रकार ग्रन्थि यानी गाँठ और अर्बुद यानी रसौली आदि में छेद शब्द इष्ट है; गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ और उदर यानी सम्भवतः पेट का रोग आदि में भेद शब्द; अतिसार यानी दस्त और रक्तपित्त यानी रक्तस्राव का रोग आदि में रुद्ध शब्द; अश्मरी यानी पथरी और उदावर्त यानी वायु का ऊपर की ओर पलटना आदि में प्रवर्तन शब्द, ऐसा।
english: Likewise, in granthi (nodule), arbuda (tumour) and the like, the word 'cutting' (cheda) is desired; in gulma (abdominal lump), udara (probably an abdominal disease) and the like, the word 'breaking' (bheda); in atisāra (diarrhoea), raktapitta (a bleeding disorder) and the like, the word 'stopped' (ruddha); in aśmarī (urinary stone), udāvarta (upward-turning of wind) and the like, the word 'impelling' (pravartana): thus.
notes: 'iṣṭaḥ' is stated once and carried to the later pairs (elliptical; no verb supplied). Identifications: granthi = nodule or cyst, arbuda = tumour (standard); gulma = abdominal lump (probable); udara here is the abdominal disease (probably the swelling of the belly), not the belly itself (probable); atisāra = diarrhoea (standard); raktapitta = a bleeding disorder (standard); aśmarī = urinary stone (standard); udāvarta = a disorder in which the downward wind is turned upward, with stoppage of stool and wind (probable). 'chedaśabdaiṣṭo' (छेदशब्दइष्टो) and 'pravarttanaśabdaiti' (प्रवर्त्तनशब्दइति) are printed with separate vowels: regular hiatus after -aḥ (śabda iṣṭaḥ, śabda iti), not typos. The doubled -rtt- of pravarttana is normalised (recorded once book-wide).
lines_deva: तथा ग्रंथ्यर्बुदादिषु छेदशब्दइष्टो गुल्मोदरादिषु भेदशब्दोऽतिसाररक्तपित्तादिषु रुद्धशब्दोऽश्मर्युदावर्तादिषु प्रवर्त्तनशब्दइति
lines_iast: tathā graṃthyarbudādiṣu chedaśabdaiṣṭo gulmodarādiṣu bhedaśabdo'tisāraraktapittādiṣu ruddhaśabdo'śmaryudāvartādiṣu pravarttanaśabdaiti

words.gloss: to be applied, to be fitted

hindi: इसी प्रकार दूसरी ध्वनियाँ भी जोड़ी जानी चाहिए।
english: In this way other sounds too are to be applied.

text_flags.why: possible: avagraha dropped after -e (anye 'pi); written as anye api in words

notes: 'yojyāḥ' (to be applied, fitted) means the sounds are to be treated by the same principle as in the preceding unit; the Sanskrit states no more.

words.gloss: firm, stationary, increasing, protected (trāta; or protector), immovable, fixed, safety, auspicious, and so on

words.gram: m. nom. pl. (read for printed anyā)

hindi: और सब जगह स्थिर, स्थावर, वर्धमान, त्रात यानी रक्षित, अचल, ध्रुव, क्षेम, शिव आदि शब्द तथा अन्य वाद्यों के स्वर श्रेष्ठ हैं।
english: And everywhere, the words sthira (firm), sthāvara (stationary), vardhamāna (increasing), trāta (protected), acala (immovable), dhruva (fixed), kṣema (safety), śiva (auspicious) and the like, and other sounds of musical instruments, are best.

text_flags.why: possible: feminine singular/plural form does not agree with masculine vāditrasvarāḥ
possible: stray anusvara after sthāvara inside the compound (or a lost space: sthāvaraṃ vardhamāna...); written without it in words

notes: 'trātā'cala' is read trāta + acala (an avagraha after ā is a print habit); 'trāta' may be 'protected' or 'protector' (trātṛ), the form is uncertain. 'anyā' (feminine) does not agree with the masculine vāditrasvarāḥ and is read anye (possible typo). The compound list is read as words (śabdāḥ) that are best; 'ca ... ca' joins the words and the instrument sounds.
lines_deva: सर्वत्रैव च स्थिरस्थावरंवर्धमानत्राताऽचलध्रुवक्षेमशिवादयः शब्दा अन्या वादित्रस्वराश्च श्रेष्ठाः
lines_iast: sarvatraiva ca sthirasthāvaraṃvardhamānatrātā'caladhruvakṣemaśivādayaḥ śabdā anyā vāditrasvarāśca śreṣṭhāḥ

words.gloss: sneeze (kṣuta), struck, fallen, outcry, blow, cutting, breaking, burning, 'hā hā', prohibition, and the like (words)
of grass, palala (sense uncertain: mud, flesh or sesame paste), a bundle of wood, a potsherd, a clod and so on

of a thorn, one with raised foot, vehicle, bed, seat and so on, broken, household articles, empty pot, madya (an intoxicating drink), fat (vasā), oil, a pregnant woman, a śvapāka (dog-cooker, outcaste), one in distress (vyasanin), the dead
from the house of the patient (conjectural, see flag)
the going out of the previously mentioned auspicious things
Ketu; Saturn (śani) (first members of a compound that goes on in the next token)
in house, wife, bed, seat, vehicle, gem, jewel, equipment

hindi: छींक, मारा गया, गिरा, चीख, प्रहार, छेद, भेद, जलना, हाहा और निषेध आदि शब्द निषिद्ध हैं; निषिद्ध और जलती हुई दिशा में पक्षियों और पशुओं की क्रूर ध्वनियाँ; या सूखे और मुरझाए, लताओं और काँटों वाले वृक्ष पर अथवा वैसे ही स्थान में; और तृण, पलल यानी कीचड़ या मांस या तिल की लुगदी, लकड़ी का बोझ, ठीकरा, ढेला आदि का, काँटे का, ऊपर उठे पैर वाले का, वाहन, शय्या, आसन आदि का, टूटा हुआ, गृहसामग्री, खाली घड़ा, मद्य यानी नशीला पेय, वसा, तेल, गर्भिणी, श्वपाक, विपत्ति में पड़े हुए और मृतों का दर्शन, प्रवेश के समय; और रोगी के घर से पहले कहे गए मंगल पदार्थों का निकलना, अनुमानित पाठ पर; और भीतर आए वैद्य का सत्कार नहीं, लाभ, सन्तोष और स्तुतियाँ, रोगी के शुभ और अशुभ; अनुमानित पाठ पर, वक्र और अनुवक्र ग्रह, निन्दित स्थानों में स्थित; केतु, शनि और राहु द्वारा जन्म नक्षत्र का दबाया जाना; घर, पत्नी, शय्या, आसन, वाहन, मणि, रत्न और उपकरणों में निन्दित लक्षणों का प्रकट होना, चिकित्सा के निषेध के लिए।
english: The words sneeze (kṣuta), struck, fallen, outcry, blow, cutting, breaking, burning, 'hā hā', prohibition and the like are forbidden; in a forbidden and in a blazing direction, cruel cries of birds and beasts; or on a dry, withered tree with creepers and thorns, or in a place of that kind; and, at the entering, the sight of grass, palala (sense uncertain: mud, flesh or sesame paste), a bundle of wood, a potsherd, a clod and so on, of a thorn, of one with raised foot, of vehicles, beds, seats and so on, broken, household articles, empty pots, madya (an intoxicating drink), fat (vasā), oil, a pregnant woman, a śvapāka (dog-cooker, outcaste), one in distress (vyasanin) and the dead; and, on a conjectural reading, the going out of the previously mentioned auspicious things from the patient's house; and for the physician who has entered, no honour, and gain, satisfaction and praises, auspicious and inauspicious (ones) of the patient; on a conjectural reading, the planets (graha) retrograde and following-retrograde (vakra, anuvakra), standing in condemned positions; the overpowering of the birth-nakṣatra by Ketu, Saturn and Rāhu; or the appearance of condemned signs in house, wife, bed, seat, vehicle, gem, jewel, equipment: for the prohibition of treatment.

text_flags.why: possible: 'a' of ātura lost, and 'pūrvīkta' for pūrvokta
possible: stray r (lābhaḥ tuṣṭi would give lābhastuṣṭi)
possible: 'yahā' for 'grahāḥ' (gra/ya confusion), since garhitasthānasthāḥ (nom. pl.) follows
possible: śini for śani (Saturn)
certain: space missing where no sandhi applies; written as separate words in words

notes: GROUPING: one very long sentence of lists; the only predicate is 'pratiṣiddhāḥ' (forbidden) in the first clause, and the rest is read as a series of omen-lists ending in 'cikitsāpratiṣedhāya' (for the prohibition of treatment, i.e. for refusing the case); no verb is supplied and the reading is low confidence. The close of the list of items seen ('tṛṇa ... mṛtānām') is read as a genitive of 'darśanam'. 'bhagna' probably qualifies the preceding yāna, śayana and āsana; 'ūrdhvapāda' may mean one standing on tiptoe or with raised feet; printed 'orddha' has a doubled dd (normalised). 'palala' has several senses (mud, flesh, sesame paste): disputed here. 'śvapāka' = outcaste, lit. dog-cooker. 'cāturgṛhāt' is read ca + āturagṛhāt (patient's house) conjecturally, and 'pūrvīkta' as pūrvokta (previously mentioned), the auspicious things being those of line 10 (card 10); 'lābhartuṣṭi' has a stray r. 'śubhāśubhā āturasya' (auspicious and inauspicious of the patient) attaches either to the preceding lābha-tuṣṭi-nutayaḥ or opens the next clause; kept literal. 'vakrānuvakrāyahā' is read vakra-anuvakrāḥ grahāḥ (vakra = retrograde motion of a planet; anuvakra = a later retrograde stage; probable), conjecturally. 'ketuśini rāhubhiḥ' is read ketu-śani-rāhubhiḥ, the compound divided by a printed space. 'savallikaṃṭake' read sa-vallika-kaṇṭake.
lines_deva: क्षुतहतपतिताक्रोशप्रहारच्छेदभेददाहहाहाप्रतिषेधादिशब्दाः प्रतिषिद्धाः प्रतिषिद्धायां दीप्तायां च दिशि क्रूराः पक्षिमृगध्वनयो वृक्षे वा रूक्षशुष्के सवल्लिकंटके तद्विधे वा देशे दर्शनं च तृणपललकाष्ठभारकर्परकलोष्टादीनां कंटकोर्द्धपादयानशयनासनादिभग्नोपस्कररिक्तकुंभमद्यवसातैलगर्भिणीश्वपाकव्यसनीमृतानां च प्रवेशे चातुर्गृहात्पूर्वीक्तमांगल्यनिर्गमः प्रविष्टस्य तु भिषजः न सत्कारो लाभर्तुष्टिनुतयश्च शुभाशुभा आतुरस्य वक्रानुवक्रायहा गर्हितस्थानस्थाः केतुशिनि राहुभिर्जन्मर्क्षाभिभवो गृहदारशयनासनवाहनमणिरत्नोपकरणेषुवा गर्हितलक्षणप्रादुर्भावश्चिकित्साप्रतिषेधाय

words.gloss: cause of the auspicious and the inauspicious

hindi: स्वप्न स्वयं या दूसरे के द्वारा देखा गया शुभ और अशुभ का कारण है। वह सात प्रकार का है: देखा हुआ, सुना हुआ, अनुभव किया हुआ, चाहा हुआ, कल्पित, भाविक यानी आगे होने वाले से सम्बन्धित, और दोषों से उत्पन्न।
english: A dream, seen by oneself or by another, is a cause of the auspicious and the inauspicious. It is of seven kinds: seen, heard, experienced, desired, imagined, bhāvika (relating to what will be), and born of the doṣas.

text_flags.why: possible: m for n (the sense needs anyena, by another)
certain: space missing where no sandhi applies; written as separate words in words

notes: 'svayamamyena' is read svayam anyena. 'prārthitaḥsaṃkalpito' has no space between the words; the visarga is kept in print. 'bhāvika' is rendered literally (a dream of what is to come); the Sanskrit gives no more. The seven kinds are named in order; the next unit says the first five are fruitless.
lines_deva: स्वप्नस्तु स्वयमम्येन वा दृष्टः शुभाशुभहेतुः स सप्तविधो दृष्टः श्रुतोऽनुभूतः प्रार्थितःसंकल्पितो भाविको दोषजश्च

words.gloss: according to one's own natural constitution (prakṛti)
in the first part of the night

hindi: उनमें पहले पाँच प्रकार निष्फल हैं; इसी प्रकार जो अपनी प्रकृति के अनुसार है, जो भूल गया, जो दिन में देखा गया, बहुत छोटा, बहुत लम्बा, और जो गहरी नींद में नहीं देखा गया; रात्रि के पहले भाग में वह थोड़ा और देर से फल देता है।
english: Among these, the first five kinds are fruitless; likewise (one) according to one's own natural constitution (prakṛti), forgotten, by day, too short, too long, and seen when not deeply asleep; in the first part of the night it gives a little fruit, and after a long time.
notes: Elliptical: after 'tathā' the list (own prakṛti, forgotten, by day, too short, too long, not seen in deep sleep) has no stated predicate; it is read as parallel to 'aphalaḥ' (fruitless), but the text does not say so and the last clause ('pūrvarātre ... phalaṃ karoti') has its own verb. 'nātisuptadṛṣṭaḥ' could also be read 'seen not when very asleep' (as rendered) or as a compound of 'not too deeply asleep'. 'ādyaḥ pañcavidhaḥ' = the first five of the seven kinds in line 20 (card 20) (seen, heard, experienced, desired, imagined).
lines_deva: तत्राद्यः पंचविधोऽफलः तथा यथास्वप्रकृतिर्विस्मृतो दिवाऽतिह्रस्वोऽतिदीर्घो नातिसुप्तदृष्टश्च पूर्वरात्रेऽल्पं चिराच्च फलं करोति
lines_iast: tatrādyaḥ paṃcavidho'phalaḥ tathā yathāsvaprakṛtirvismṛto divā'tihrasvo'tidīrgho nātisuptadṛṣṭaśca pūrvarātre'lpaṃ cirācca phalaṃ karoti

words.gloss: at daybreak (the time of letting out the cows)

hindi: गोसर्ग यानी प्रातः काल में महान और तुरन्त।
english: At gosarga (daybreak, the time cows are let out), great and at once.

text_flags.why: certain: space missing where no sandhi applies; written as separate words in words

notes: Elliptical; the noun that is 'great' is not stated (presumably the fruit, phalam, of line 21 (card 21)) and none is supplied. 'gosarga' is the early morning.

words.gloss: by giving, appeasing (śamanīya) and so on

hindi: और फिर नींद से, या विपरीत वचनों से, या दान, शमनीय यानी शान्त करने वाले आदि से नष्ट न किया गया।
english: And not struck down again by sleep, or by contrary words, or by giving, appeasing (śamanīya) and the like.

text_flags.why: possible: stray m inside śamanīya-m-ādibhiḥ
certain: space missing where no sandhi applies; written as separate words in words

notes: Continues line 22 (card 22) (no subject is stated; the dream is understood). 'anupahataḥ' = not cancelled. The printed 'dānaśamanīyamādibhirvā' has a stray m (śamanīya-m-ādibhiḥ) and is read dāna-śamanīya-ādibhiḥ. śamanīya = appeasing or pacifying acts.

hindi: उनमें जो प्रेतों के साथ मद्य यानी नशीला पेय पीता हुआ कुत्ते द्वारा खींचा जाता है, वह ज्वर यानी बुखार से आहत होता है।
english: Among these, he who, drinking madya (an intoxicating drink) with the departed (pretas), is dragged by a dog, is struck down by fever (jvara).
notes: 'hanyate' (is struck down) can also mean 'is killed'; the more literal 'struck down' is kept. jvara = fever (standard). preta = a departed spirit.
lines_deva: तत्र यः प्रेतैः सह मद्यं पिबन् शुना ऽऽकृष्यते स हन्यते ज्वरेण
lines_iast: tatra yaḥ pretaiḥ saha madyaṃ piban śunā ''kṛṣyate sa hanyate jvareṇa

words.gloss: of the hue of red lac
with red body, garland and cloth

hindi: जो लाख के लाल रंग जैसा अम्बर यानी वस्त्र या आकाश देखता है, अथवा जो लाल देह, माला और वस्त्र वाला हँसता हुआ स्त्री द्वारा ले जाया जाता है, वह रक्तपित्त यानी रक्तस्राव के रोग से।
english: He who sees an ambara (garment or sky) of the hue of red lac, or who, with red body, garland and cloth, laughing, is carried off by a woman, he by raktapitta (a bleeding disorder).

notes: GROUPING: 35 and 36 appear to continue one sentence: 36 gives the contrast for the healthy (verb carried over). The whole unit is one long printed line with many yaḥ-clauses (each 'who …') and closes with 'te vyādhitāḥ pañcatām āpnuvanti'; the clauses are all marked by vā/ca, so the semicolons in the translation are an editorial division. Readings: 'abhyavahṛtya' = eating or swallowing (kept as in the glossary). 'chardayati' (vomits) and 'viricyate' (is purged, passive) kept distinct. 'srotasā' here is a water-current, not the body channel. 'dig-vāsāḥ' (sky-clothed) = naked. 'kapi-ratha' (monkey-chariot) relation of the compound is not stated. 'valmīka-…-āyatana': śvabhra-āyatana could also be one tat-puruṣa ('pit-abodes'); the dvandva list is taken. 'paṅka-kūpa-kaluṣa-udaka': could also be 'mud, well, turbid water' as three or four members; taken as a list. 'saṃbādha' read as noun 'confined place'; 'jananī' is 'mother' (a womb is not stated). 'śmaśru-karma' is literally beard-work (not further explained). 'yūpa-puṣpa-āḍhya-śālmalī-…': puṣpāḍhya (flower-rich) may qualify the following trees ('flower-rich śālmalī, …') instead of standing as a separate member; the plain list reading is taken. 'labhate vā hiraṇya…kārpāsān aśnāti pakvānnaṃ': taken as 'obtains gold…cotton; eats cooked food'. Alternatively aśnāti takes the whole list (eats gold, iron, salt, oil, oil-cake, cotton) as well as the cooked food; the sandhi 'kārpāsān aśnāti' allows both. 'daśana' in the series moon … eyes, teeth = teeth. 'anyatamān' is plural ('any of'); 'naśyataḥ' accusative plural participle. 'vakraṃ vā bāhuṃ nagnaṃ vā vibhidyamānaṃ': vibhidyamānam may agree with vakram, bāhum or nagnam; translated as printed (see text_flags). 'kaṣāya-vāsasaḥ': kaṣāya here is a colour (reddish-brown, ochre), not a taste (standard sense of the word). 'śukla-darśanā' = of white appearance; daśanā 'white-toothed' is a possible alternative, not adopted. 'dīrgha-keśa-stanīm': dīrgha may qualify hair only or hair and breasts. Kālarātri here = form of 'dark night'. 'pañcatā' = the euphemism for death. Identifications (modern names beside the Sanskrit): śālmalī = Bombax ceiba (standard). kiṃśuka = Butea monosperma, palāśa (standard). kovidāra = Bauhinia variegata (probable). pāribhadraka = Erythrina variegata (probable; the name is also used for other trees). vetra = cane, rattan, Calamus (probable). vaṃśa = bamboo (standard). kārpāsa = cotton, Gossypium (standard). śaṣkulī = a fried cake (probable; the word also means the ear-orifice, not here). Draviḍa and Āndhra are kept as names (in standard use peoples of the south). Print habits (recorded here once): b for v (bayāṃsi = vayāṃsi, prabrajita = pravrajita); a double avagraha ('' ) printed after -ā in ''kṛṣyate is a print habit, not an elision. Regular sandhi (digvāsā, pariṣvajyate nagno) needs no flag. 'dakṣiṇābhimukham ākṛṣyate': the adverb may mean 'dragged toward the south' rather than 'facing south'; both readings are possible and the translation keeps 'facing south'. 'srotasā vāhriyate' is read vā hriyate (is carried off by a current); vā āhriyate is also possible.
lines_deva: यः शष्कुलीरपूपान्वाऽभ्यवहृत्य प्रतिबुद्धश्छर्दयतियस्य शिरसि लतादयो जायंते बयांसि च निलीयंते मौढ्यं वा भवतियो गृध्रोलूककाकाद्यैः प्रेतपिशाचरक्षोद्रविडांध्रस्त्रीचंडालाद्यै र्वा परिचर्यते दक्षिणाभिमुखं वा स्त्रिया नृत्यंत्या ऽऽकृष्यते वायसादिभिर्वा स्वयंवा दिग्वासा याति शून्याटवीं वा कपिरथेन प्रेतैः प्रब्रजितैर्वा परिष्वज्यतेनग्नो वा रक्तां स्रजं धारयति पंकदिग्धो हसति नृत्यति वा वेत्रवंशकंटकतृणगहने संसृज्यते पतति वा पांशूपधानायां भुवि वल्मीकभस्मश्मशानश्वभ्रायतनेषु वा पंककूपकलुषोदकेषु वा मज्जति स्रोतसा वाह्रियते रक्तकुसुमवनांभूमिं गुहामंधकाराचितां पापकर्मालयं संबाधंजननीं वा प्रविशति मत्स्येन वा ग्रस्यते श्मश्रुकर्म च यो गात्रवृद्धिंविवाहं चानुभवति शैलप्रासादाग्रात्पत्यारोहति वा यूपपुष्पाढ्यशाल्मलीकिंशुककोविदारपारिभद्रकान् यो वा पराजीयते बध्यते छर्दयतिविरिच्यते हृष्यति लभते वा हिरण्यलोहलवणतैलपिण्याककार्पासानश्नाति पक्वान्नं पिबति मद्यं स्नेहं वा ऽभ्यज्यते निर्भर्त्स्यते वा कुपितैःपितृभिः चंद्रार्कतारादीपदेवतानेत्रदशनान्यतमान्नश्यतो वा पश्यतिवक्रं वा बाहुं नग्नं वा विभिद्यमानं पुरुषान् वा नग्नान्कषायवाससोऽसौम्यान्दंडपाशहस्तान् कृष्णान् रक्ताक्षान् स्त्रियं वा कृष्णां शुक्लदर्शनां दीर्घकेशस्तनीं कालरात्रिरूपां ते व्याधिताः पंचतामाप्नुवंति
lines_iast: yaḥ śaṣkulīrapūpānvā'bhyavahṛtya pratibuddhaśchardayatiyasya śirasi latādayo jāyaṃte bayāṃsi ca nilīyaṃte mauḍhyaṃ vā bhavatiyo gṛdhrolūkakākādyaiḥ pretapiśācarakṣodraviḍāṃdhrastrīcaṃḍālādyai rvā paricaryate dakṣiṇābhimukhaṃ vā striyā nṛtyaṃtyā ''kṛṣyate vāyasādibhirvā svayaṃvā digvāsā yāti śūnyāṭavīṃ vā kapirathena pretaiḥ prabrajitairvā pariṣvajyatenagno vā raktāṃ srajaṃ dhārayati paṃkadigdho hasati nṛtyati vā vetravaṃśakaṃṭakatṛṇagahane saṃsṛjyate patati vā pāṃśūpadhānāyāṃ bhuvi valmīkabhasmaśmaśānaśvabhrāyataneṣu vā paṃkakūpakaluṣodakeṣu vā majjati srotasā vāhriyate raktakusumavanāṃbhūmiṃ guhāmaṃdhakārācitāṃ pāpakarmālayaṃ saṃbādhaṃjananīṃ vā praviśati matsyena vā grasyate śmaśrukarma ca yo gātravṛddhiṃvivāhaṃ cānubhavati śailaprāsādāgrātpatyārohati vā yūpapuṣpāḍhyaśālmalīkiṃśukakovidārapāribhadrakān yo vā parājīyate badhyate chardayativiricyate hṛṣyati labhate vā hiraṇyalohalavaṇatailapiṇyākakārpāsānaśnāti pakvānnaṃ pibati madyaṃ snehaṃ vā 'bhyajyate nirbhartsyate vā kupitaiḥpitṛbhiḥ caṃdrārkatārādīpadevatānetradaśanānyatamānnaśyato vā paśyativakraṃ vā bāhuṃ nagnaṃ vā vibhidyamānaṃ puruṣān vā nagnānkaṣāyavāsaso'saumyāndaṃḍapāśahastān kṛṣṇān raktākṣān striyaṃ vā kṛṣṇāṃ śukladarśanāṃ dīrghakeśastanīṃ kālarātrirūpāṃ te vyādhitāḥ paṃcatāmāpnuvaṃti

hindi: किन्तु स्वस्थ, जीवन के सन्देह को।
english: But the healthy (ones): a doubt about life.
notes: GROUPING: 36 appears to continue 35: the verb (āpnuvanti, 'attain') is carried over from 35 and is not supplied in the translation (elliptical line). The closing 'iti' ('thus') ends the statement begun in 35. 'svasthāḥ' is taken as the plural of the healthy (ones); 'jīvita-saṃdeham' as accusative, the object of the carried verb.

hindi: और इस विषय में ये हैं:
english: And on this matter there are:
notes: Lead-in formula 'bhavanti cātra' ('and here there are'), which in this treatise introduces the verses that follow (38 onward); nothing is supplied after 'bhavanti' in the translation.

hindi: मन को वहन करने वाले स्रोतस् यानी मार्गों के प्रबल मलों यानी अपशिष्ट से भरे होने के कारण विनाश की ओर उन्मुख आत्मा वालों द्वारा भयंकर स्वप्न देखे जाते हैं।
english: Because of the fullness of the mind-carrying channels (srotas) with powerful malas (waste matter), Terrible dreams are seen by (ones) whose selves are turned toward destruction.
notes: [02.12.38] GROUPING: 38 and 39 appear to form one sentence (38 gives the reason, 39 the statement). 'srotas' (channel) and 'mala' (waste, impurity) are doctrinal terms and kept; whether mala here means the doṣas is not stated. 'manovaha' is taken as 'mind-carrying' (qualifying srotasām). [02.12.39] GROUPING: appears to complete the sentence begun in 38. 'svapnā' = svapnāḥ (regular loss of visarga before v).

hindi: अशुभ स्वप्न को भी देखकर जो वहीं फिर से सौम्य और शुभ को देखे, तो उसके लिए फल शुभ ही हो।
english: One who, having seen even an inauspicious dream, right there again should see a gentle, auspicious (one), for him the result would be auspicious indeed.
notes: [02.12.40] GROUPING: 40 and 41 form one sentence (the verb paśyet is in 41). 'tatra eva' is taken as 'right there' (in that very place or in that same sleep); the text does not say which. [02.12.41] GROUPING: completes the sentence of 40. 'saumyam śubham' stand for an unstated noun (the dream is understood from 40), shown as '(one)'.
lines_deva: अकल्याणमपि स्वप्नं दृष्ट्वा तत्रैव यः पुनः
पश्येत्सौम्यं शुभं तस्य शुभमेव फलं भवेत्
lines_iast: akalyāṇamapi svapnaṃ dṛṣṭvā tatraiva yaḥ punaḥ
paśyetsaumyaṃ śubhaṃ tasya śubhameva phalaṃ bhavet

hindi: देवताओं को, द्विज यानी दो बार जन्म लेने वालों को, गायों और बैलों को, जीवित मित्रों को, राजाओं को सज्जनों को, यशस्वियों को, प्रज्वलित अग्नि को, अत्यन्त स्वच्छ जलाशयों को
english: Gods (deva), twice-born (dvija), cows and bulls, living friends, kings, Good men (sādhu), famous (ones), a kindled fire, very clear water-bodies (jalāśaya),

text_flags.why: certain: nh for hn is a letter reversal (cf. vha/hva); vahni 'fire' is certain from the sense and the metre is unchanged

notes: [02.12.42] GROUPING: 42 to 45 are lists of accusatives with no verb in them; they appear to be objects of 'paśyet' in 46 (or continue 41). 'go-vṛṣabha' is taken as a dvandva 'cows and bulls'; 'bull (go-vṛṣabha)' as one word is also possible. 'suhṛdo nṛpān' = suhṛdaḥ nṛpān. [02.12.43] GROUPING: continues the list of 42. 'yaśasvinaḥ' stands for an unstated noun, so '(ones)'.

hindi: कन्या को, कुमारों को, गोरों को, श्वेत वस्त्र वालों को, अत्यन्त तेजस्वियों को नरभक्षी को, दीप्त शरीर वाले को, चारों ओर से रक्त से सींचे हुए को
english: A maiden, boys, fair (ones), white-clothed (ones), very radiant (ones), a man-eating (one), a blazing-bodied (one), sprinkled with blood all around,
notes: [02.12.44] GROUPING: continues the list of 42. 'gaurān', 'śuklavastrān' and 'sutejasaḥ' may qualify 'kumārakān' (boys) instead of standing as separate members; read here as separate members with the unstated noun shown as '(ones)'. [02.12.45] GROUPING: continues the list of 42; the verb is in 46 (paśyet). The three words may describe one figure or three; the text does not say which. 'narāśana' is literally 'man-eating'; no particular being is named.

hindi: जो देखे, या जो पाता है, छत्र यानी छाता, आदर्श यानी दर्पण और अस्पष्ट शब्द विशामिष श्वेत पुष्प, वस्त्र, अमेध्य यानी अशुद्ध का लेप, फल
english: He who should see, or who obtains, an umbrella (chatra), a mirror (ādarśa) and viśāmiṣa (unclear) White flowers (sumanas), cloth, a smearing with impure (matter), fruit,

text_flags.why: possible: 'viśāmiṣam' does not give a clear word; ś/ṣ confusion is common, and viṣ (excrement) or viṣa (poison) with āmiṣa (flesh) are conceivable; no reading is adopted and the word is left unclear

notes: [02.12.46] GROUPING: the list of 42-45 appears to be the object of 'paśyet' here, and the list of 46-47 of 'labhate'. 'viśāmiṣam' is left unsplit and unclear (the guesses are in the text_flag only); the first two members chatra, ādarśa are clear. The printed form 'paśyellabhate' = paśyet labhate. [02.12.47] GROUPING: continues 46; these are objects of 'labhate' (obtains). 'amedhya' = unfit, impure; the substance is not named, shown as '(matter)'. 'sumanas' = flower here (it can also name jasmine; not stated).

words.gloss: mountain; palace; with fruit; tree; lion; man; elephant (dvipa, lit. 'twice-drinker')

hindi: पर्वतों, महलों, फलदार वृक्षों, सिंहों, मनुष्यों और हाथियों को चढ़े, और घोड़े के वाहन पर, और अनुमानित पाठ पर नदों, झीलों और समुद्रों को पार करे
english: Mountains, palaces, fruit-bearing trees, lions, men, elephants, Should climb (them) and a horse-vehicle, and, on a conjectural reading, should cross rivers, lakes (hrada) and oceans (udadhi).

text_flags.why: possible: 'hada' (r dropped) and 'nadan' do not give the expected nouns; nadān hradodadhīn (rivers, lakes, oceans) fits the sense (the pāda has 8 syllables either way, so metre is no evidence); adopted on a conjectural reading

notes: [02.12.48] GROUPING: these accusatives are the objects of 'ārohet' ('should climb') in 49. [02.12.49] GROUPING: completes the construction of 48 ('ārohet' takes 48 and the horse-vehicle). The reading 'hrada' (lake, pool) is conjectural; 'nada' (river) is the masculine word, plural 'nadān'. 'taret' is optative of √tṝ (cross, swim across).

words.gloss: star; mountain; radiant (ones), also the sun

hindi: पूर्वोत्तर से गमन, अगम्य के पास जाना, मृत्यु संकीर्ण स्थान से निकलना, तारों, पर्वतों और प्रकाशमानों का स्पर्श
english: Going by the east-north (north-east), approaching the unapproachable, death, Emerging from a confined place, the touching of stars, mountains and radiant (ones),
notes: [02.12.50] GROUPING: 50 to 52 are further nominal items with no verb of their own; the governing verb (paśyet of 46, or syāt of 53) is not in these units, and the case forms are mixed (mṛtim accusative, niḥsṛtiḥ nominative). 'pūrvottareṇa' is the instrumental of 'east-north', i.e. the north-east direction. 'agamyāgamana' literally 'approaching the unapproachable'; in law-texts it names intercourse with a forbidden woman, which this line does not say. [02.12.51] GROUPING: continues 50. 'bhāsvat' means radiant and is also a name of the sun; the translation keeps 'radiant (ones)'.

hindi: रोना, गिरे हुए का उठना और शत्रुओं का मर्दन यानी कुचलना जिसके लिए आयु, आरोग्य और धन हो, वह बार-बार अनुमानित पाठ पर पाता है।
english: Weeping, the rising of one who has fallen, and the crushing of enemies, he for whom there would be life, health (ārogya) and wealth, he often attains, on a conjectural reading.

text_flags.why: certain: space missing where no sandhi applies; written as separate words in words
possible: 'aśrute' (a-śrute, 'in the unheard') gives no clear sense after 'bahuśaḥ'; aśnute 'attains, enjoys' fits the sentence and the metre; adopted on a conjectural reading

notes: [02.12.52] GROUPING: continues 50-51 and appears to lead into 53. 'dviṣatām' is the genitive plural participle used as a noun ('of those who hate'). [02.12.53] GROUPING: 50-53 appear to be one construction: a list of dream-events followed by this statement. The syntax is not clear: 'yasya syāt …' may mean that the listed things occur for him, with āyuḥ, ārogyam, vittam as further members, and the object of 'aśnute' is not stated. Taken in the plainest way; confidence low. Alternative parse: 'yasya syāt' may close the relative clause (the items of 50-52 occur for him), with 'āyur-ārogyaṃ vittam' as accusative objects of 'aśnute' ('he obtains life, health and wealth, often'); this would give aśnute an object and fits the adopted conjecture. Translation kept as drafted; owner to decide.

hindi: क्रुद्ध, भयभीत और कृश स्वरूप वाले पितरों, देवताओं और द्विजातियों के मैले वस्त्र और फूलों वालों के दर्शन की प्रशंसा नहीं की जाती।
english: Of forefathers (pitṛ), gods (deva) and twice-born (dvijāti) who are angry, frightened and emaciated in person, of (ones) with dirty garments and flowers, the sight is not praised.
notes: [02.12.54] GROUPING: 54 and 55 form one sentence (54 gives the possessors, 55 the verb). 'ātman' at the end of the bahuvrīhi is read as 'in person' (the self or person of those described). [02.12.55] GROUPING: completes the sentence begun in 54; the genitive 'malina-ambara-puṣpāṇām' joins 54's list of persons by asyndeton and no 'and' is supplied in the translation; the compound may instead qualify the same forefathers, gods and twice-born as a further adjective (cf. 56).

hindi: किन्तु उन्हीं सन्तुष्टों के, शुद्ध पुष्प और वस्त्र वाले स्वरूप वालों के स्वप्न में दर्शन की प्रशंसा की जाती है, और उनके साथ बातचीत शुभ है।
english: But of those very (ones) when pleased, pure in person with flowers and garments, the sight is praised in a dream, and conversation with them is auspicious.
notes: [02.12.56] GROUPING: 56 and 57 form one sentence (56 gives the genitives, 57 the statement). The compound 'śuddha-puṣpa-ambara-ātman' could also mean 'of pure self, with flowers and garments'; the plainer reading is taken. [02.12.57] Completes 56. 'śasyate' (passive of √śaṃs, metre 8 syllables) is the same verb as 'praśasyate' in 55 without the prefix; not a typo. In the second clause the copula is understood.
lines_deva: दर्शनं शस्यते स्वप्ने तैश्च संभाषणं शुभं
lines_iast: darśanaṃ śasyate svapne taiśca saṃbhāṣaṇaṃ śubhaṃ

words.gloss: sesame seeds (tila, Sesamum indicum; standard; conjectural; printed tvilān)

hindi: भयंकर या शोभन यानी अच्छे स्वप्नों को देखकर, प्रातः स्नान किया हुआ, अस्पष्ट शब्द सर्पषानमिवर्णान सावित्री मन्त्र से घी में सने हुओं को या अनुमानित पाठ पर तिलों को हवन करके, पवित्र हुआ पापों से और रोगों से मुक्त हो जाता है।
english: Having seen terrible or good (śobhana) dreams, bathed in the morning, sarpaṣānamivarṇān (unclear), having offered with the Sāvitrī (a sacred verse) (ones) smeared with ghee, or, on a conjectural reading, sesame seeds, purified, one is freed from sins and from diseases.

text_flags.why: certain: m for n; svapnān 'dreams' is required by the sense (cf. svapnaṃ in 40)
garbled: 'sarpaṣā' is not a form; the ending -varṇān (m. acc. pl.) is clear. A conceivable start is sarpiṣā (with ghee) or sarṣapān (mustard seeds), but no reading is adopted
possible: 'tvilān' is not a word; tilān (sesame seeds) fits an offering smeared with ghee; adopted on a conjectural reading. The double avagraha after -ā is a print habit

notes: [02.12.58] GROUPING: 58 and 59 form one sentence (the verb 'mucyate' is in 59). The last word is left unsplit and unclear (the guesses are in the text_flag only); its ending -varṇān is an accusative plural and may be the object of 'hutvā' in 59, which also has an accusative plural 'āktān'. 'śobhana' is read as 'good, auspicious'. [02.12.59] GROUPING: completes the sentence of 58. The object of 'hutvā' is not clear: 'āktān' (smeared) agrees with an accusative plural, which may be the damaged word at the end of 58 or 'tilān'; the plain reading 'smeared (ones), or sesame seeds' is taken. 'sāvitryā' is the Sāvitrī verse (not further identified here). 'pūtaḥ' purified; 'mucyate' takes the instrumental. The subject is not stated ('one'). Alternative parse: 'sarpiṣā āktān tilān' = 'sesame seeds smeared with ghee' (āktān as adjective of tilān), which needs no supplied '(ones)'; the damaged word of 58 may be a second object. sāvitrī = the Sāvitrī verse, i.e. the Gāyatrī addressed to Savitṛ (standard). Translation kept as drafted; owner to decide.
lines_deva: दृष्ट्वा स्वप्मान् दारुणान्शोभनान्वा प्रातः स्नातः सर्पषानमिवर्णान्
हुत्वा सावित्र्या सर्पिषाऽऽक्तांस्त्विलान्वा पूतः पापैर्मुच्यते व्याधिभिश्च
lines_iast: dṛṣṭvā svapmān dāruṇānśobhanānvā prātaḥ snātaḥ sarpaṣānamivarṇān
hutvā sāvitryā sarpiṣā''ktāṃstvilānvā pūtaḥ pāpairmucyate vyādhibhiśca

hindi: मंगल आचार से युक्त परिवार, और वैसे ही रोगी श्रद्धावान्, अनुकूल और प्रचुर द्रव्यों के संग्रह वाला
english: The retinue endowed with auspicious conduct, and likewise the patient (ātura), Having faith, favourable, and having an abundant collection of materials (dravya),

text_flags.why: certain: space missing where no sandhi applies; written as separate words in words

notes: [02.12.60] GROUPING: 60 to 63 appear to be one list of signs (nominal items without verbs) ending with 63: 'that is the sign of ārogya'. The singular 'saṃpannaḥ' may qualify both retinue and patient; 'parivāra' is taken as the people around the patient. The '' in 'tathā''turaḥ' is a print habit (tathā āturaḥ). [02.12.61] GROUPING: continues 60. 'dravya' (material, substance) is not specified further in the text.

words.gloss: sattva (a quality of mind); mark; association

hindi: सत्त्व यानी मन के गुण के लक्षणों का संयोग, वैद्यों और द्विजातियों में भक्ति चिकित्सा में निराश न होना: वह आरोग्य यानी स्वास्थ्य का लक्षण है।
english: Association with the marks of sattva (a quality of mind), devotion to physicians and twice-born, Non-despondency in treatment: that is the sign of health (ārogya).
notes: [02.12.62] GROUPING: continues 60-61. 'sattva' is a doctrinal term and kept; the text gives no further definition. [02.12.63] GROUPING: completes the list of 60-62; 'tad' refers to the signs just listed. Copula understood. 'a-nirveda' = absence of weariness or despair.
